transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I’ve gotten into this habit of making myself throw up after I eat, and I can’t seem to stop doing it even though I know it’s not right. It is really hard for me to admit this, but it has gotten to the point where I just don't know how to handle it on my own anymore.

Do you ever have episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short time and feel out of control, and are you doing this mainly because you are very afraid of gaining weight or because of how you feel about your body?

Yes, on stressful nights I'll stand at the kitchen counter and plow through half a pizza, chips, and leftovers in twenty minutes, feeling like a switch flipped and I just can't stop. I do it because I'm absolutely terrified of gaining weight; if my work coveralls feel tight or my face looks puffy next to the younger techs, I feel like a failure who doesn't deserve my lead role.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F50.2, F50.4, F50.8]. Based on the new information, the patient describes recurrent binge eating with loss of control followed by self-induced vomiting, and the behavior is clearly driven by intense fear of weight gain and body-image overvaluation. This makes the bulimic pattern most likely. F50.4 is less likely because the eating disturbance is not occurring in the context of a primary depressive syndrome, and F50.8 is less likely because the presentation is no longer atypical or unspecified given the classic binge–purge pattern.
